feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid evidence of scope across strategy, platforms, and operations. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with tighter structure, fewer repeated skills sections, and more quantified outcomes tied to business results.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support “Digital Communications & Strategy Lead.”  
- Good credibility and scope: NACo progression shows advancement, leadership, platform ownership, and technical depth across Drupal, analytics, email, and multimedia.  
- Writing is polished and mostly error-free, with strong action verbs and concrete scale indicators like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views.”

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve scannability and make the CV feel sharper.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities well, but more results would strengthen impact (e.g., traffic growth, email performance, production savings, engagement lifts, team size, budget size).  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; punctuation in lists is slightly inconsistent; “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “French (A2, learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV, but it is slightly generic and repeats language already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding one or two concrete signals of seniority would make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience.”
- Lead with current senior value: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems for mission-driven organizations.
- Trim channel list slightly to avoid sounding like a skills inventory; emphasize outcomes and leadership instead.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, and the workflows, governance, and systems that enable effective digital operations at scale. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The channel list repeats details already reinforced throughout Work Experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the summary, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and pluralize for consistency: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform administration,” “Analytics and performance reporting.”
- Shift from task-level wording to higher-value scope: “Digital transformation and platform modernization” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation.”
- Replace vague items with sharper leadership language: “Stakeholder and cross-functional alignment” or “Editorial governance and workflow design.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation & platform modernization • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics, insights & performance reporting • Workflow systems architecture • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or using it only for broad themes.
- “Stakeholder coordination” and “policy/advocacy communication” are already covered in the header summary.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and Recent Projects. Make it sharper by foregrounding scope, ownership, and 2–3 concrete outcomes or flagship builds.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter summary: “Embedded full-time as a strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, analytics, and AI-enabled search.”
- Collapse overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-led bullets; start with verbs like Led, Built, Designed, Advised.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages/users, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, publishing efficiency gains, search accuracy/discovery improvements, stakeholder groups supported.
- Example phrasing: “Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components, enabling reusable member-facing toolkits and faster campaign launches.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI-enabled search, microsites, anniversary campaign, and advocacy video work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry focused on role-level ownership, not project detail.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also echo the header and NACo roles; avoid repeating generic “support/advised on digital strategy” language.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia production, and budget oversight across web, email, social, and video.”
- Prioritize the highest-impact bullets first: website migration, analytics stack expansion, and in-house studio build.
- Add outcome language where possible: e.g., “standardized publishing across 50+ internal publishers,” “improved reporting speed/visibility for leadership,” or “reduced reliance on external production vendors,” if accurate.
- Tighten channel bullet phrasing: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and other public-sector stakeholders.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version higher-level and strategic.
- Video-programming language overlaps with both earlier NACo roles and Recent Projects; emphasize studio build and operational scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what you owned before stepping into broader strategy/management.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter scope statement: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and advocacy video, improving editorial coordination and publishing consistency.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add a measurable workflow/editorial outcome if available, such as publishing volume, turnaround time, campaign cadence, or number of cross-functional teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/coordination” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Video-series language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and Recent Projects; keep this version centered on scaling an existing recurring program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive value rather than repeating broad digital/comms terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and stakeholder messaging
- Audience strategy and content planning
- Consider swapping “multi-channel communications leadership” for “content operations” or “digital transformation” to better reflect recent director/consulting work.
- If space allows, make one line outcome-oriented, e.g., “Enterprise web strategy for 10,000+ page, 3.5M annual-view platform.”
- Keep wording parallel: noun phrases only, avoid mixing leadership traits with tactical activities.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize current, differentiating strengths tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool dump to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop weaker/older or lower-signal items here: remove jQuery unless it is still actively used in recent roles.
- Consider moving secondary platforms to Technical + IT only; keep this topline section focused on strongest, most marketable platforms.
- If space allows, add light scope language: “Enterprise Drupal platforms” or “Large public-sector web ecosystems” to reinforce seniority and context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already appear in Core Competencies.
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages are repeated in Technical + IT; avoid listing the same tools in full in both places.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT. This Topline Skills item should emphasize strategic analytics capability, not repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity • SEO and performance analysis”
- Put the highest-value, recent strengths first: KPI design, reporting infrastructure, and decision support before individual tools.
- Tighten wording: change “Leadership reporting” to “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for stronger business language.
- If space allows, add outcome-oriented language: “analytics infrastructure and executive dashboards” to better connect skills to impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the Technical + IT “Data, Analytics & Optimization” section; keep tools here minimal and save the fuller stack for Technical + IT.
- GA4/Clarity/Power BI/Looker Studio/BigQuery are already substantiated in the 2022–2024 Director role, so avoid overloading this line with the same list.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus several NACo experience bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and production environment rather than repeating broad video terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery
- Tighten and sharpen the list: Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and webcast production • PTZ camera and switching workflows • Studio buildout and operations • Hybrid, virtual and live event delivery

- Keep terms aligned with recent experience, especially the in-house studio build and advocacy/event programming at NACo

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Video production and editing” is partly covered by “Multimedia & Creative Tools” and multiple work-experience bullets.
- “Livestreaming” duplicates Core Competencies wording; use “webcast production” or “live event delivery” to differentiate.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” skills section. This item should either add proficiency/context or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show depth and recency: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, group by strength: “Primary: Drupal, WordPress • Working knowledge: SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages”
- Consider removing GitHub Pages unless it supports a notable project; it reads lighter than the enterprise platforms.
- Keep platform names only; don’t repeat “CMS modernization” here since that already appears elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles and projects, so avoid repeating it in multiple sections without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second phrase for modern delivery/integration work: “Technical systems: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, strengthen with scope/context instead of just tools, e.g. “for Drupal-based public websites, campaign microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the CV uses version-specific naming; “HTML, CSS” is cleaner

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”). Differentiate by framing this as hands-on implementation tools, not another summary list
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” if space is tight

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for faster scanning: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier • Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp • Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If true, add light context instead of only listing tools: “Workflow automation, project tracking and cross-team collaboration tools”
- Prioritize the strongest/recently relevant tools first; if Airtable and Power Automate are most used, keep them leading and consider dropping one lower-value PM tool to tighten

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep only if they support the workflow-systems positioning or trim for space

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is relevant to the candidate’s recent leadership in email operations, but it’s currently just a vendor list and misses the strategic/enterprise angle shown elsewhere in the CV. It should signal platform ownership and scale without repeating newsletter details from NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If space allows, add light context: Enterprise email campaign delivery • Member communications platforms • Journey automation
- Keep the list to the strongest/current tools only; lead with Dynamics 365 and Higher Logic if those are most recent/relevant

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid adding “newsletters,” “tens of thousands,” or channel-management claims here; those are already covered in recent work experience
- Don’t repeat generic “multi-channel communications” language already captured in Core Competencies and Topline Skills

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and useful scope, but it reads broadly and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete outputs or scale you can add.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add specific outcomes if available: website traffic, livestream/event volume, video cadence, email growth, or production turnaround improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence to highlight distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a clearer management phrase if accurate: “mentored” or “supervised” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on launching/establishing the format, not scaling it.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the later NACo roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast as the clearest differentiator and tighten the rest.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more specific support function, e.g., “produced multimedia and digital content to support research, program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, internal stakeholders supported, audience growth, or whether the podcast established a new recurring channel.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad multimedia/digital production language already covered more strongly in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize team leadership here if that growth is better demonstrated in later positions.
